topic: Jacob & Monod Model, Negative Inducer Control, & Catabolite Repression
quickSummary: Lac operon (E. coli, Jacob & Monod 1961): polycistronic unit with i gene (repressor), promoter, operator, and structural genes z (beta-galactosidase), y (permease), and a (transacetylase). Dual regulation: Negative control via allolactose (inducer detaches repressor); Positive control via cAMP-CAP complex (low glucose stimulates maximal transcription).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: The Lac Operon governs lactose catabolism in E. coli. Consists of i gene (homotetrameric repressor), Promoter, Operator, and 3 structural genes: z (beta-galactosidase), y (permease), a (transacetylase). Negative regulation: allolactose (inducer) binds repressor, detaching it from the operator. Positive regulation: low glucose elevates cAMP, which binds CAP to promote maximal RNA polymerase binding.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 9.1 Structural & Regulatory Genes of the *Lac* Operon
1. **$i$ Gene**: Regulatory gene encoding the **Lac Repressor** protein (homotetramer), expressed constitutively.
2. **$z$ Gene**: Encodes **$\beta$-Galactosidase**, which cleaves lactose into glucose and galactose, and converts a small fraction to **allolactose** (the true inducer).
3. **$y$ Gene**: Encodes **$\beta$-Galactoside Permease**, increasing membrane permeability to lactose.
4. **$a$ Gene**: Encodes **$\beta$-Galactoside Transacetylase**, transferring acetyl groups to toxic $\beta$-galactosides.

### 9.2 Dual Regulatory Control

```
                        NEGATIVE CONTROL (INDUCER EFFECT)
                        
   NO LACTOSE (Repressed):
   Repressor binds Operator ──► Blocks RNA Polymerase ──► Operon OFF (No Transcription)
   
   LACTOSE PRESENT (Induced):
   Allolactose (Inducer) binds Repressor ──► Conformational Shift ──► Repressor detaches from Operator
   ──► RNA Polymerase transcribes z, y, a ──► Operon ON
```

```
                   POSITIVE CONTROL (CATABOLITE REPRESSION)
                   
   HIGH GLUCOSE (Low cAMP):
   CAP / CRP remains INACTIVE ──► Weak RNA Pol binding ──► BASAL / LOW Transcription
   
   LOW GLUCOSE + HIGH LACTOSE (High cAMP):
   cAMP binds CAP ──► Active cAMP-CAP Complex binds CAP site ──► MAXIMAL Operon Expression
```

conceptBreakdown.heading: Gratuitous Inducer: IPTG
conceptBreakdown.title: Gratuitous Inducer: IPTG
conceptBreakdown.content: Isopropyl-beta-D-thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG) is a gratuitous inducer that binds and inactivates the Lac repressor without being metabolized by beta-galactosidase, keeping the operon continuously ON in laboratory research.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Basal Leaky Expression of the Lac Operon
conceptBreakdown.title: Basal Leaky Expression of the Lac Operon
conceptBreakdown.content: A repressed Lac operon is never 100% OFF; a tiny basal level of permease and beta-galactosidase must be present in the cell membrane to allow the first few molecules of lactose to enter and be converted into allolactose.
